Sources: 8-K exhibits 99.1 (release) and 99.2 (presentation) of 12 November, 2Q26 10-Q, 9 November preview. Four quarters of public history (IPO October 2025).
changes: TensorWave lease and AMD credit support terminated (release). The anchor of the bull case is gone.

Replacement: an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for 600 MW from 2027, with a $200mn prepayment agreement, a $15mn early-works agreement and a $90mn steel purchase still being finalized; no definitive lease.

Cash $315.5mn incl. restricted (from $91.7mn) after the $431mn convert; debt (net of issuance costs) $958.4mn; burn ~$188mn a quarter (operating ~$54.5mn, about double the 1H pace, plus PP&E ~$133mn) gives under two quarters of runway before the prepayment (our calc).
Loss jumped to $141.6mn from $25.8mn, mostly non-cash: $65.8mn stock comp and $21.5mn of advisory fees paid in stock.

31 December deadlines (Keystone prepayment trigger, Texas Tech notice to proceed) not updated; F-class EPC still in negotiation; Hillcore BOOT framework (up to ~2.6 GW, $0 Fermi capex) still shown, definitive documents not confirmed.

consensus_thesis: Brokers rate Fermi a Buy as an option on scarce Texas power assets and a signed TensorWave lease; at ~$1.6-1.8 before results the tape priced distress or heavy dilution (Provisional); shares rose ~17% pre-market on the hyperscaler news.
headline: The consensus view should move from 'a signed lease waiting for financing' to 'an unsigned hyperscaler LOI racing a cash clock': tenant quality and scale improved, but nothing is yet binding and credit quality weakens until a definitive lease and project debt exist.
kona: Fermi swapped a signed lease with a neocloud and vendor credit support for an unsigned investment-grade hyperscaler offering a prepayment: hyperscalers will pay early to reserve behind-the-meter power, but lenders lend on leases, not letters. Kona should treat a tenant prepayment as bridge capital only, avoid land or loan deadlines that depend on a lease date it does not control, and contract the power plant (EPC, turbines) before promising first-power dates.

name: Fermi America

sections.body: Emphasized more: investment-grade hyperscaler, 'speed to power', owned gas generation (2,000 MW) and a 2027-2029 power ramp. Less or dropped: TensorWave and AMD; the 1 July 2027 first-power date (per preview). KPIs more important: cash runway, prepayment receipts, EPC award dates. Risks up: tenant concentration (one unnamed tenant for all 2027 power). Down: tenant credit quality. → A single investment-grade tenant for 600 MW is a better financing base than TensorWave was, but until it signs a lease, lenders have nothing to lend against.

sections.body: $mn. Funding gap = PP&E additions plus operating burn (our calc). The 2Q 10-Q put 12-month Phase 0-1 capex at about $2bn, possibly over $3bn. What the next dollar costs: secured equipment debt at 12-13%; the convert at 5% is the cheapest paper but sits behind ~$570mn of secured loans. Maturities in 24 months: MUFG ~$445mn (August 2027). Per-share: market cap ~$1.16bn at $2.11 pre-market on 12 November (GuruFocus, ~7:00 a.m. ET; ~$1.81 on 11 November, derived) against book PP&E $1.67bn. → A signed IG lease would let Fermi raise project debt at a fraction of 12%; without it, the next dollar is equity at a depressed price.

sections.title: Five signals

head: Question
Why it matters
rows: The release lists a $200mn prepayment agreement with the hyperscaler but no lease. When is the cash due, is it refundable if no lease is signed, and is it conditional on a first-power date?
Does the hyperscaler agreement count as an 'approved customer agreement' for Keystone and a 200 MW Phase 1 lease for Texas Tech before 31 December? If not, are waivers agreed?
Cash was $315.5mn and burn about $188mn last quarter. How many months of runway, and is an equity raise planned before the lease signs?
The first-power date of 1 July 2027 is no longer in the materials. What is the date for the first MW to the hyperscaler, and when is the F-class EPC awarded?
Why were TensorWave and AMD terminated rather than extended, and were any fees paid or received?
Is the board running a sale or strategic review after the 30 October vote, and what is the status of the EDNY and SEC requests?
